s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal and pelvic pain with a renal mass and vascular involvement
salient_findings: Right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation
Visible vessels extending into the renal cortex
Fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein
key_facts: Right renal mass located in the upper pole
Visible vessels extending into the renal cortex
Fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein
Thrombus extending to the confluence with the inferior vena cava
No other masses or enlarged lymph nodes identified

s4.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension

raw.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension
raw.rationale: The presence of a renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, and a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to the inferior vena cava are characteristic of renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension.

rejected.label: Angiomyolipoma with renal vein thrombosis
rejected.why: While angiomyolipomas can contain fat and have vascular components, the presence of a tumor thrombus in the renal vein and inferior vena cava is more suggestive of a malignant process like renal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a subtype of renal cell carcinoma, but the provided information does not specifically suggest clear cell histology.

rejected.label: Renal metastasis from endometrial carcinoma
rejected.why: The description of the renal mass and its extension into the renal vein and inferior vena cava does not typically match the pattern of metastatic disease.

rejected.label: Papillary renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: This subtype of renal cell carcinoma is less likely given the presence of fat attenuation within the mass, which is more characteristic of clear cell renal cell carcinoma or other types with fatty components.
